react_result.final_narrative_text: The nine differentially abundant metabolites converge powerfully on galactose metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. Cross-paradigm consensus is strong: RaMP ORA returned the KEGG:native pathway 'map00052' alongside the SMPDB synonym 'SMP00043' both at rank 1 with FDR=8.76e-15 (fold enrichment ~1500), and the KEGG human-specific analogue 'hsa00052' scored p=5.65e-09 in MetaboAnalystR PSEA. Mummichog independently recovered the same functional module as 'MUMM:galactose_metabolism' at rank 3 with p=0.00538 and 11 overlapping compounds. The five driver metabolites are sucrose (KEGG:C00089), galactinol (KEGG:C01235), galactitol (KEGG:C01697), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116). These map onto the Leloir pathway: galactinol is the galactose donor to myo-inositol (galactinol synthase reaction), sucrose feeds free galactose downstream, and galactitol is the polyol shunt product of galactose reduction. Glycerol appears as a shared intermediate between galactose and glycerophospholipid metabolism. Aspirin (KEGG:C01405), methionine sulfoxide (KEGG:C02989), and allysine (KEGG:C04076) do not participate in the galactose cluster and instead drive separate Reactome hits for transport of small molecules and lipid metabolism, indicating a secondary effect. The near-perfect InChIKey first-block clustering across the five galactose metabolites (distinct connectivity clusters) rules out structural artefact, confirming a true biological signal centred on galactose handling.

Cross-paradigm consensus is strong: RaMP ORA returned the KEGG:native pathway 'map00052' alongside the SMPDB synonym 'SMP00043' both at rank 1 with FDR=8.76e-15 (fold enrichment ~1500), and the KEGG human-specific analogue 'hsa00052' scored p=5.65e-09 in MetaboAnalystR PSEA. Mummichog independently recovered the same functional module as 'MUMM:galactose_metabolism' at rank 3 with p=0.00538 and 11 overlapping compounds. The five driver metabolites are sucrose (KEGG:C00089), galactinol (KEGG:C01235), galactitol (KEGG:C01697), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116). These map onto the Leloir pathway: galactinol is the galactose donor to myo-inositol (galactinol synthase reaction), sucrose feeds free galactose downstream, and galactitol is the polyol shunt product of galactose reduction. Glycerol appears as a shared intermediate between galactose and glycerophospholipid metabolism. Aspirin (KEGG:C01405), methionine sulfoxide (KEGG:C02989), and allysine (KEGG:C04076) do not participate in the galactose cluster and instead drive separate Reactome hits for transport of small molecules and lipid metabolism, indicating a secondary effect. The near-perfect InChIKey first-block clustering across the five galactose metabolites (distinct connectivity clusters) rules out structural artefact, confirming a true biological signal centred on galactose handling.
